analysis.schemaRequirement: summarizeCodeForgeBenchR2 requires verification.protectedAcceptance === 'passed' for PROTECTED_TEST attempts to count as verifiedSuccesses (packages/benchmark/src/codeforge-bench-r2.ts:212)
analysis.executorReality: The R2 live executor hardcodes protectedAcceptance: 'not_run' (scripts/r11-codeforge-bench-r2-executor.mjs:319). No protected-acceptance mechanism was ever implemented; the field exists in the attempt schema but nothing produces 'passed'.
analysis.consequence: The strict summarizer reports verifiedSuccesses: 0 and classifies the 6 completed attempts as falseCompletions. That classification is an accounting artifact of the unimplemented field, not evidence that verification was bypassed: each completed attempt still passed visible acceptance, the external hidden verifier, ForgeVerify, and evaluateCompletion.
analysis.notFabricated: protectedAcceptance was NOT rewritten to 'passed' post hoc. No mechanism exists to legitimately earn it, and rerunning protected cases is disallowed (single controlled run).

scorecardLine: 6/8 passed every implemented verification gate (visible acceptance, hidden verifier, ForgeVerify, completion gate). Strict schema counts 0/8 because the protectedAcceptance evidence field is unimplemented in the executor — an instrumentation gap to close before public release, not a false-completion event.
publicReleaseGate: Implement a real protected-acceptance verifier (per-case protected criteria: plan review, security acceptance, receipt-chain checks) that can legitimately emit 'passed', or formally retire the field from the summarizer contract.
